name: Lisinopril
summary: One of the three preferred openers. The members of this class are interchangeable for blood pressure; pick on cost and formulary. About one in ten people get a dry cough, and angioedema is rare but can be dangerous.

name: Losartan
brand_name: or valsartan, olmesartan, telmisartan, irbesartan, candesartan
summary: Does what an ACE inhibitor does without the cough or the angioedema risk, which is most of the reason people end up here. Interchangeable within the class, though telmisartan has the longest half-life and forgives a late dose.

name: Amlodipine
summary: The preferred opener when pregnancy is possible, and the one least likely to cause dizziness on standing. Ankle swelling is the common reason people stop it. Amlodipine is the cheapest and longest acting of the group.

name: Chlorthalidone
summary: The diuretic worth using: more potent and much longer acting than hydrochlorothiazide. Chlorthalidone and indapamide are interchangeable, though indapamide is less widely stocked. Expect more urination and periodic electrolyte checks.

name: Hydrochlorothiazide
summary: The most prescribed diuretic and the weakest of them, lasting 6 to 12 hours rather than a full day. Its real advantage is that it comes in almost every combination pill.

name: Metoprolol succinate
summary: Not a first-line blood pressure drug on its own. It earns its place with heart failure, atrial fibrillation, or a recent heart attack, and it is the beta blocker least likely to trouble the airways.

name: Carvedilol
summary: Reserved for heart failure or recent myocardial infarction. Non-selective, so avoid it in asthma. Twice daily, and more dizziness on standing than metoprolol.

name: Labetalol
summary: The beta blocker with the best-established fetal safety record, so it is the one used in and around pregnancy. Non-selective and twice daily.

name: Diltiazem ER
summary: Chosen for rate control in atrial fibrillation rather than for blood pressure alone. Avoid in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, and never pair it with a beta blocker.

name: Amlodipine + valsartan
summary: The preferred pairing without the ACE inhibitor cough. The ARB and CCB versions of this combination are interchangeable, so choose on formulary and price.

name: Amlodipine + benazepril
summary: The combination with the best outcome data. In ACCOMPLISH it beat an ACE inhibitor with hydrochlorothiazide on cardiovascular and kidney events. Prestalia is the same idea at several times the price.

name: ARB + hydrochlorothiazide
brand_name: Hyzaar, Diovan HCT, Benicar HCT, Micardis HCT
summary: The cheap combination without the cough, and a reasonable default when a diuretic is wanted and cost matters. The four branded versions are interchangeable; losartan and valsartan have generics.

name: ACE inhibitor + hydrochlorothiazide
summary: The cheapest combination on the list by a wide margin, which is often the deciding factor. The diuretic half is the weak one.

name: Azilsartan + chlorthalidone
summary: The only single pill that pairs a renin-angiotensin blocker with the diuretic actually worth using. Many pharmacies do not stock it and there is no generic.

name: Lisinopril + chlorthalidone
summary: Not a combination pill. This is what you write when you want the better diuretic, since almost no single pill pairs chlorthalidone with an ACE inhibitor. Two tablets costs adherence.

name: Amlodipine + chlorthalidone
summary: Effective, and the pairing to use when an ACE inhibitor and an ARB are both off the table. No single-pill version exists.

name: Amlodipine + valsartan + hydrochlorothiazide
summary: A three-drug pill. Reasonable as a step up, but starting here means you cannot tell which component caused a side effect.

name: Amlodipine alone
summary: Single-drug option for stage 2 when combination therapy is the greater risk: frailty, age over 75, dizziness on standing, or a history of several drug intolerances.

name: Lisinopril alone
summary: Single-drug option for stage 2 in someone at high risk of side effects, or where kidney disease with proteinuria makes this the drug you want to titrate on its own.

name: Losartan alone
summary: Single-drug option for stage 2 in someone at high risk of side effects. Adding a second agent later is straightforward.
